outlooks.summary: Scattered large hail events, a few of which may be significant, are likely from the Texas Big Country into southwest Oklahoma between 3 pm to 12 am CDT. Isolated to scattered severe wind gusts and a brief tornado or two are also possible.

sections.title: Southern Great Plains
sections.text: Have amplified the probabilities resulting in a hail-driven upgrade to Enhanced risk given the likelihood of numerous storms along the dryline this afternoon and evening. Large hail should be the predominant hazard (some of which could be significant) given wind profiles favoring initially semi-discrete supercells evolving into multiple clusters, with unremarkable low-level winds limiting the tornado hazard. A surface cyclone over south-central KS will weaken as it tracks into northern MO this evening, with the dryline mixing across western OK and remaining nearly stationary across the eastern Permian Basin. With pervasive low to mid 60s surface dew points ahead of the dryline and ample diabatic heating across TX, a plume of MLCAPE from 1500-2500 J/kg should develop by mid-afternoon amid steep 700-500 mb lapse rates around 7-8 C/km. While low-level wind profiles will be weak and exhibit veer-back-veer tendency with height, deep-layer speed shear will be strong with effective values from 50-60 kt. Guidance is rather consistent in suggesting extensive storm development along the dryline by late afternoon and evening. This setup should favor several initially semi-discrete supercells

sections.text: Aside from some minor line adjustments -- particularly over the Texas South Plains area where dry air has spread into portions of the SLGT and ENH risk areas behind the surface boundary -- the ongoing forecast/reasoning remains valid. outlooks.summary: Scattered thunderstorms associated with large hail and wind damage will be possible this evening across parts of western, central and north Texas. Marginally severe thunderstorms will also be possible across parts of eastern Oklahoma and northwest Arkansas.

sections.title: Southern Plains
sections.text: Latest radar imagery shows scattered severe storms across north Texas extending to near the Red River. The storms are located along the northeastern edge of a corridor of instability where the RAP is estimating MLCAPE in the 500 to 1000 J/kg range. At mid-levels, water vapor imagery shows a subtle shortwave trough embedded in southwest flow near the Red River in far southern Oklahoma. This feature along with strong deep-layer shear and increasing low-level flow will help maintain convective development into mid evening across north Texas into far southern Oklahoma where isolated large hail and some damaging wind gusts will be possible. Further southwestward across west-central Texas, a couple supercells are ongoing to the north of San Angelo. These storms are located along a corridor of moderate instability where the RAP is estimating MLCAPE from 1000 to 2000 J/kg. The instability along with strong deep-layer shear evident on the San Angelo WSR-88D VWP, should be sufficient to maintain supercell development over the next couple of hours. Supercells with large hail are expected to continue moving northeastward into the northeastern part of the enhanced risk area over the next couple

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms are forecast to develop between 19-22Z. Large hail will be the primary severe risk. Isolated severe gusts are possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Midday subjective surface mesoanalysis places a southwest-northeast oriented dryline from the Permian Basin into southwest OK and north into west-central OK. Temperatures range from the lower-middle 80s degrees F near the US 83 corridor to the lower 70s in central OK. Surface dewpoints range from the middle 60s in southwest OK to the lower 60s where temperatures are the warmest and greatest mixing has occurred. As the boundary layer continues to heat, the remaining weak convective inhibition will continue to erode and convective initiation is forecast in a general sense by mid afternoon (19Z-20Z). A moderately unstable airmass (MLCAPE ranging from 1500 northeast to 2500 J/kg near the Red River) amidst a strong 0-6 km shear (65 kt) will support an initial threat for supercells to evolve with a risk for large to very large hail. Later in the convective cycle, modification of the thermal profile coupled with additional storms developing largely parallel to the dryline will result in a gradual tempering of the hail threat. Isolated severe gusts are also possible with the storms. The risk for a brief/weak tornado will likely be minimized given the already observed reduction in the low-level hodograph per KDYX and KFDR VAD data and the models showing no hodograph enlargement given the veer-back-veer wind profile here-forward.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Widely scattered to scattered thunderstorms may develop over this corridor through 00Z, with hail being the dominant threat, and isolated damaging gusts also possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Surface mesoanalysis at 18Z depicted a mesolow over southwestern OK near FDR, with dryline southwestward to near BPG then arching across east-central Pecos County and into northern Coahuila. Some eastward motion of the northern part of the dryline is likely, while the portion roughly south of I-20 stalls and then retreats this evening. Mass convergence and diurnal heating will continue to erode MLCINH near the dryline and contribute to increasing potential for sustained/surface-based thunderstorms through the remainder of the afternoon. East of the dryline, 12-14 g/kg mean mixing ratios and 7-7.5 deg C/km low/middle-level lapse rates will contribute to 2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE, amidst 50-60-kt southwesterly effective-shear vectors. Those vectors and mean winds oriented nearly parallel to the dryline indicate potential for a relatively quick transition to quasi-linear/messy modes, but with some early-stage supercellular characteristics enhancing updraft strength and contributing to hail growth. Increasing CINH and decreasing low-level mass convergence with southwestward extent will limit coverage to some extent in the next few hours. Need for a watch (along with timing and extent) still is uncertain, given concerns over convective coverage/duration in this region during the remainder of the afternoon. A separate round of strong-severe thunderstorms should develop this evening as well, as a series of mid/upper-level vorticity maxima eject from the southeastern quadrant of the southwestern U.S. cyclone, overlying a moistening, strengthening fetch of low-level flow from near the Rio Grande.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A localized hail/wind risk will continue from the I-44 Red River Valley region southwestward into the TX Big Country.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar imagery during the mid afternoon shows a broken band of storms acquiring a messy convective morphology across western north-central TX into southwest OK. The parallel orientation of the mean flow/dryline will likely exacerbate the ability for storms with the cluster of storms southwest of Wichita Falls to become better organized and yield an otherwise greater hail risk. Further complicating longer-term severe possibilities across this region is the northward advection of a well-mixed but drier boundary layer (surface dewpoints ranging from 56-61 degrees F) from south of I-20 northward to the Red River Valley. A gradual reduction in buoyancy will result and serve as an overall limiting factor towards more vigorous updrafts/severe potential. Farther south in the Big Country, discrete storm mode will likely continue for the next several hours until stronger forcing for ascent arrives later this evening. Higher potential for severe hail will likely exist with any thunderstorm during the next 0-2 hour period in this mesoscale area compared to farther northeast. ..Smith.. 03/26/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: While thunderstorm coverage may remain limited over the next few hours, an increase in coverage is expected this evening with the potential for large hail and isolated damaging wind gusts.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Regional radar and satellite data from 2230Z depicts a dearth of thunderstorm activity over most of Severe Thunderstorm Watch #20 across West Texas -- with the exception of Glasscock county. The latest objective analysis coupled with surface analysis suggests the limited coverage may be the result of weak low-level convergence and enhanced CIN. While WW 20 may remain devoid of thunderstorm activity over the next few hours, thunderstorms are expected to increase in coverage later this evening. This should occur as a series of mid-level impulses impinge on the area and overlap a moistening air mass with strengthening low-level flow. This is supported by high-resolution CAM guidance, which suggests rapid storm initiation around 02-03Z this evening along the dryline/cold front intersection or nearby any residual outflow boundaries from earlier activity. Large hail and isolated damaging wind gusts are expected to be the primary severe hazard with this activity as it progresses northeastward overnight. ..Elliott.. 03/26/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for large hail -- some significant -- and isolated damaging wind gusts remains over the next few hours across northwest Texas into portions of southern Oklahoma.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest radar/satellite data from 2350Z indicated two primary areas of ongoing stronger convection across Severe Thunderstorm Watch #19. The most intense activity is associated with two semi-discrete supercell thunderstorms over southwestern portions of WW #19 and far northern portions of WW #20. These storms have shown persistent severe MRMS MESH hail cores over the last hour. Surface/objective analysis places this activity along the western edge of the moisture gradient and within an area of large hail-growth-zone CAPE and strong deep-layer effective bulk shear in excess of 50 knots. Large hail -- with some significant hail -- and isolated damaging wind gusts remain likely with this activity as it shifts northeastward over the next few hours. Another area of strong thunderstorms is beginning to shift into southern Oklahoma. While MRMS MESH data suggest updrafts across this area have been less persistent -- owing to a messier storm mode -- at least isolated instances of large hail will remain possible as this activity shifts into portions of far southern Oklahoma -- near the Red River -- over the next few hours. ..Elliott.. 03/26/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorm coverage is expected to increase over the next few hours across WW #20 over portions of West Texas, with the potential for large hail and isolated damaging wind gusts continuing into the overnight. Meanwhile, isolated/periodic instances of large hail and damaging wind gusts remain possible across portions WW #19 over the Texas Big Country into far southern Oklahoma over the next hour or so, as thunderstorms continue to gradually weaken. While WW #19 will likely be allowed to expire on-time at 0200Z, a few counties near Abilene may be added to Watch #20.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Regional radar, satellite, and lightning data depict a weakening trend in thunderstorm activity across portions of the Texas Big Country into southwest Oklahoma over the last hour. This is occurring as the air mass over this area continues to stabilize in the wake of repetitive bouts of air mass overturning from widespread convection. While a few instances of near-severe hail remain possible over the next hour or so, WW #19 will likely be allowed to expire as scheduled at 0200Z. As expected, thunderstorms are beginning to increase in coverage/intensity across WW #20 near the Edwards Plateau and eastern portions of the Permian Basin. This is occurring as a mid-level vorticity maxima ejects toward the area and intersects strengthening moist southeasterly low-level flow. Expect thunderstorms to gradually intensify over the next few hours across this area, with large hail and isolated wind damage remaining the primary severe hazards into the overnight. Some counties across southern portions of Watch #19 may be added to Watch #20. ..Elliott.. 03/27/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe storms will remain possible into the overnight across parts of southwest to northwest TX, generally 25 miles either side of a line from Terrell to Throckmorton Counties. Although storms will persist overnight, the presence of marginal instability suggests the overall severe-weather threat should continue to diminish.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Trends in radar and IR satellite imagery and lightning data indicated the strongest storms were located in the northern extent of WW 20, generally from Coke County to Jones County. Forcing for ascent attendant to a midlevel impulse tracking east/northeast into southwest and west TX through tonight will support additional thunderstorm development within a low-level confluence zone along the western extent of a surface moisture gradient. Effective bulk shear will remain favorable for organized storms, though storm interactions and overall marginal instability should promote a further weakening trend in the severity of the storms. ..Peters.. 03/27/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
